clue.text: If this, MD becomes master and it's a terrible thing!

parts.note: the entry splits into a statement that the letter D equals the letters ASTER; swap the D of MD for those five letters and master appears

explanation.surface: A promoted managing director turns out to be a dreadful boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If this' asks what condition would turn MD into MASTER: the D must stand for ASTER. Say that condition as three words and run them together.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a catastrophe or calamity is a terrible thing.

clue.text: Control the affairs of unpleasant court

parts.note: dire means dreadful or very unpleasant
Ct is the abbreviation for court, as in street addresses

explanation.surface: Someone takes charge of a nasty tribunal's business.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to manage or run an organisation is to control its affairs.

clue.text: Scholar has a vehicle in street

indicators.note: in places the article and the vehicle between the two letters of the street abbreviation

parts.note: a van is a goods vehicle

explanation.surface: A learned person keeps a car parked on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a learned person of deep knowledge is a scholar.

clue.text: Oarsman in trouble in republic

indicators.note: to trouble something is to disturb it, so the nine letters before it are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rower gets into difficulties in a foreign state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' is the anagram signal, and the first 'in' belongs to the fodder with 'Oarsman'; the second 'in' only joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this tiny landlocked state surrounded by Italy calls itself the world's oldest republic.

clue.text: You want a great deal of odour and elegance? Spray this around!

definitions.text: You want a great deal of odour and elegance? Spray this around!

indicators.note: spraying scatters droplets in all directions, so the letters named earlier are scattered into a new order
a great deal of a word is most of it, here all but the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
the last letter of odour, left out because only most of the word is used
taken as written

explanation.surface: An advert promises fragrance and style to anyone who sprays the product about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a great deal of' trims odour to ODOU, and 'Spray this around' is the anagram signal for ODOU plus ELEGANCE. The whole clue also describes the answer, so it is its own definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a light perfume is sprayed on to smell pleasant and feel refined.

clue.text: Still it can shock and ruin the reception

definitions.text: it can shock and ruin the reception
definitions.meaning: the electrical charge that gives a small jolt from a door handle, and the crackle that spoils a radio or television signal

explanation.surface: A motionless guest manages to scandalise everyone and spoil the wedding party.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: motionless as an adjective, and as a noun the electrical charge and the crackling interference on a broadcast.

clue.text: Roots about trunk

indicators.note: about suggests the letters being moved around into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tree roots spread around the base of the trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the trunk is the body without head and limbs.

clue.text: Lightly touch steward forgetting one cheap drink

parts.note: to tap is to touch lightly

indicators.note: forgetting something means leaving it behind, so the steward word loses the letter that follows

parts.note: a steward serves food and drink, as a waiter does
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A diner nudges a forgetful attendant about an inexpensive beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting' removes I (one) from WAITER, leaving WATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: what comes from the kitchen faucet costs next to nothing to drink.

clue.text: Ship used as escort — victory travelling to Crete without it

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so the rearranged letters go around the victory letter
travelling means moving about, so the letters of the two words after it change places

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
V is the abbreviation for victory, as in VE Day

explanation.surface: A convoy vessel sails for a Greek island, where a win is no longer within reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' has its old sense of outside rather than lacking, and 'travelling' is the anagram signal. The final 'it' just points back to victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small fast warship of this class was built to guard convoys.

clue.text: Extremely hungry birds outside Oxford university

indicators.note: outside says the birds go around the letters for the university

parts.note: ravens are large black birds of the crow family

explanation.surface: Starving birds gather by the gates of an ancient college.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: famished or starving means extremely hungry.

clue.text: Decent rugby player about to make a comeback

parts.note: a prop is a forward in the front row of a rugby scrum

indicators.note: coming back means returning, so the two-letter word for about is read from its end

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in the heading of a letter

explanation.surface: A respectable sportsman is on the point of returning to the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a signal for going round something, but here it supplies letters, and 'to make a comeback' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: respectable or seemly behaviour is decent behaviour.

clue.text: Focussing attention on notice before landing

indicators.note: before says the word for notice is written ahead of the word for landing

parts.note: to spot something is to notice it
to light is to come down and settle, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.surface: Passengers study a sign shortly before the plane touches down.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: highlighting something, as a stage lamp picks out a performer, focuses attention on it.

clue.text: Tory leader of grantham at a dance

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, the party whose members are called Tories

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

explanation.surface: A Conservative chief from a Lincolnshire town attends a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at Margaret Thatcher, the Conservative prime minister born in the English town of Grantham; 'at' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a party routine of Cuban origin in which people form a long winding line.

clue.text: Spies endlessly go off with an Egyptian to get their stuff

indicators.note: off can mean gone bad or out of order, so the letters gathered before and after it are put in a new order
endlessly means without its end, so the word before it loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
the final letter of Spies, which is dropped
taken as written
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for Egyptian, as in the currency sign for the Egyptian pound

explanation.surface: Secret agents keep leaving with a man from Cairo to collect their belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their' points back to the spies, so the definition is what spies do. 'off' is the anagram signal and 'endlessly' drops the last letter of the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: spying is what secret agents do, their particular line of work.

clue.text: Stick up a number of times for old school punishment

definitions.text: Stick up a number of times for old school punishment

parts.words: Stick up a number of times for old school punishment
parts.note: the stick is a teacher's cane, raised a fixed number of times to beat a pupil, as was once done in British schools

explanation.surface: A robber holds up the same place repeatedly and gets an old-fashioned penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick up' suggests an armed robbery, but the stick is a cane going up for each stroke. The phrase was British school slang for a caning of half a dozen strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: British school slang for a caning of half a dozen strokes.

clue.text: English monarch carrying handle with lines for craftsman

indicators.note: carrying says the letters for English monarch hold the handle and the lines between them

parts.note: ER is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth, Elizabeth Regina
handle is slang for a name
L is the abbreviation for line, so two lines give two of them

explanation.surface: An English king bears a ruled staff intended for an artisan.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a person who decorates metal or pottery with a glassy coating is a skilled craftsman.

clue.text: Harshly criticise fold wanting one electronic organ

parts.note: to pan a film or book is to review it savagely

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, and one says just a single copy of the following letter is missing from the fold word

parts.note: a crease is a fold pressed into cloth or paper
E is the prefix for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A reviewer savages a church congregation that has no keyboard instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'electronic organ' reads as one instrument but splits between wordplay and definition; 'wanting one' takes a single copy of that letter from the fold word.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the gland behind the stomach that makes insulin is a bodily organ.

clue.text: Neat square

definitions.meaning: of a spirit, drunk without water or mixer
honest and above board, as in a square deal

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: undiluted, as of whisky, and honest or conventional, as of a person or a deal.

clue.text: It's great being related to the stars

definitions.meaning: huge, as said informally of a price or a number
belonging to the science that studies the heavens

explanation.surface: Someone boasts how wonderful it is to have celebrity relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: informally enormous, as of a cost, and literally belonging to the science of the heavens.

clue.text: Rock star runs inside to get something for his guitar

indicators.note: inside says the letter for runs goes within the musician's name

parts.note: Sting is the English singer and bass player who fronted The Police
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A musician dashes indoors to fetch a spare part for his instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: each of the wires plucked on the instrument is one of these.

clue.text: Mark's right to pester

parts.note: a badge is a distinguishing mark or emblem; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A man called Mark is entitled to be a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to nag or harass someone persistently is to pester them.

clue.text: Singer's banter in church

parts.note: chaff is light-hearted teasing

explanation.surface: A member of the choir jokes around during the service.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a common European songbird, and crosswords call any songbird a singer.

clue.text: Criminal? 26 on this won't make a decision!

definitions.meaning: slang for a dealer who buys and sells stolen goods

definitions.text: 26 on this won't make a decision
definitions.meaning: the answer at 26 across is a person who sits, and someone who sits on this barrier refuses to take either side

explanation.surface: A crook facing a jury of twenty-six will never get a verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 stands for the answer at 26 across; the idiom of sitting on this means staying neutral.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a receiver of stolen goods, and the barrier an undecided person is said to perch on.

clue.text: Run over someone in a crowd scene

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a run not scored off the bat, such as a bye or a wide
a film performer hired to fill the background

explanation.surface: A driver knocks down a bystander during a mob sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: a cricket score not made off the bat, surplus, and a background film performer.

clue.text: Mallard, perhaps, starts to eat nuts and edges round trap

indicators.note: round says the three opening letters go around the word for a trap
the starts of words are their opening letters, here of eat, nuts and edges

parts.note: a gin is a snare for catching game

explanation.surface: A duck begins feeding on nuts and sidles around a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: Mallard is not the duck here but a famous British steam locomotive, holder of the world speed record for steam.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a railway locomotive is commonly called this, and the record-breaking Mallard is one.

clue.text: I find leg looking rotten in the covers?

indicators.note: something rotten has broken down, so the letters of the three words before it are broken up and reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone in bed pulls back the sheets and sees a limb in a nasty state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking rotten' is the anagram signal for I FIND LEG. The covers are a cricket position on the off side, so a player stationed there is doing this; the question mark admits it is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a cricketer stationed in the covers is on the side trying to stop and catch the ball.

clue.text: It's a piece of cake being an artist's model

definitions.meaning: something very easy, such as a simple catch or an open goal in sport
a person who poses for a portrait

explanation.surface: Posing for a painter turns out to be easy work.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an easy chance or task, and a person posing for a portrait.

clue.text: Repeatedly use a cloth over jelly

indicators.note: repeatedly says the four letters built by the rest of the wordplay are written out twice
over means turned over, so the word for a cloth is read from its end

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: Someone keeps wiping a spilt dessert with a duster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns RAG into GAR, which follows A; 'Repeatedly' then doubles those four letters. 'use' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a setting agent made from seaweed, used in cooking and as a laboratory culture medium.
